resources.string: ElevenLabs Scribe turns your speech into text as you talk; Claude can then tidy it up. Your audio and text go to those services under your own API keys, which are stored encrypted on this phone.
Allow the microphone in Voicebar settings
Needs speech-to-text access. Create one at elevenlabs.io under Developers → API keys.
Removes filler words, fixes punctuation and applies spoken corrections (\"Tuesday, no, Wednesday\"), with Claude Haiku or GPT-6 Luna.
The fastest model works best here.
Paste a new key to replace the saved one
Couldn\'t store the key securely on this phone
Words appear in the text field as you talk, and the polished version replaces them when it\'s ready. Off: words preview in the voice bar and are typed when you finish. Password fields always preview.

Millennial mode: dictated messages never end with a period, because a final period reads as cold. Question marks, exclamation marks and periods between sentences stay. Keep talking after a message and its period comes back before the new words.
Search fields and address bars, where a final period becomes part of what you search for.
Messages, WhatsApp, Signal, Slack… and any box whose Enter key sends. Email, notes and everything else keep their periods.
No final period in any field. Covers the two above.
Always proper punctuation. Clears the others.
While dictating, say “voice bar” and a command as the last thing, then pause. The command runs and isn\'t typed.

While a keyboard is up and you\'re not dictating (Voicebar\'s bar, or Gboard with the way-back button), the phone listens for “voice bar”. The button turns purple; “…listen” (or dictate, start, talk) starts dictating, switching back from Gboard if needed; “…close” (or hide) puts the keyboard away. Runs on the phone, nothing is sent anywhere, and the mic indicator stays on while it listens. Now: %1$s

“Voice bar, done”: finish (polished)
“Voice bar, send”: finish, then send
“Voice bar, keyboard”: finish, then Gboard
“Voice bar, clean up”: polish so far, keep listening
“Voice bar, cancel”: throw it away
“Voice bar, close”: finish, then hide the keyboard
Loose wording works too: “finish”, “send it”, “type”, “polish”, “never mind”, “scratch that”…

Dictation finishes by itself after this long without a recognized word (background noise doesn\'t count). Halfway there (at most 5 seconds in) what you\'ve said so far is cleaned up while it keeps listening; keep talking and the next cleanup sees both, so corrections still work.
Layout, typing with Gboard, the way back
Names and terms it has learned · %1$d

When you fix a name or term in what Voicebar typed (here or in Gboard), Claude checks whether it\'s worth remembering, and it\'s added here with a note you can tap to undo. Rewording and ordinary edits are ignored; password fields are never read.
Sends your 50 most used words to ElevenLabs with each dictation so they\'re heard right the first time (ElevenLabs charges a little extra for this). The cleanup always gets the whole dictionary.

Stored on this phone only. Learned mishearings are fixed by the cleanup with context; ones you added, or that came up twice, are also replaced every time. Fix a word\'s capitals by hand twice (LOL to lol), or add it here in its own capitals (lol, iPhone), and it\'s always written that way.
Millennial mode: no final period in searches, chats or everywhere
A text box to practice in
Add an ElevenLabs key to start
A few quick steps: Voicebar for talking, Gboard for typing, and a button on Gboard that brings you back.
Tap Voice and talk. Tap ABC to type on Voicebar\'s keyboard, or hold it to hand over to Gboard.
Drag to move · hold, then drag to select
Selecting · keep a finger down, drag with another to go further
no list price known for that model, so its tokens are counted but not priced

Estimated from what this phone sent, at list prices: Scribe v2 Realtime at $%1$.2f per hour of audio, and %2$s at %3$s. Plan allowances, free hours and credits aren\'t taken into account, so your actual bill can be lower; the ElevenLabs and Claude Console dashboards have the real numbers. Only counts are kept here, never your words or audio.
Create one at elevenlabs.io under Developers → API keys, with speech-to-text access, and paste it here.
Create one at console.anthropic.com under API keys and paste it here.

Tap Voice and talk; the words go straight into the field. Pause and what you\'ve said is polished while it keeps listening. Tap the pill to finish (always polished), swipe it right to finish and send, or swipe it left to throw it away. ⌫ keeps working while you talk. Or say “voice bar, done” (or send, keyboard, clean up, cancel) at the end. It also finishes by itself after a stretch of silence. Slide sideways on the idle Voice pill to move the cursor.

Tap ⌫ to delete a character; tap then hold to keep deleting. ☰ is always the menu; the other keys around Cursor, ABC and Voice (space, ⌫ and ↵ unless you change them) are yours to choose: hold one to pick, and it stays that way.
Tap Voice and talk; tap ABC to type, or hold it for Gboard.
Swipe typing crashed the keyboard, so it\'s off (Look › Swipe to type)
Swipe typing couldn\'t start (see Settings › Logs)
Slide across the letters of a word without lifting. Powered by FUTO Swipe.
A full keyboard with suggestions pops up and takes over the bar\'s row; pull its handle down to bring the bar back. Hold ABC for Gboard.
Gboard takes over for typing. Hold ABC for Voicebar\'s keyboard.
Across the bottom of the screen
A small pill: ☰, Cursor, ABC, Voice and one key you choose. From ☰ you can shrink it to just the record button, and drag that anywhere
Opens a palette of marks: your recent ones, then three pages to swipe. Hold a dotted mark for more, like curly quotes and dashes
A new line, or the box\'s own Send, Search or Go. While you dictate, always a line break
A space; slide it sideways to move the cursor
Pastes what you last copied. While you dictate it goes in at the cursor and what you\'ve said is kept
Undoes the last change, as Ctrl+Z does. Most apps support it; a few ignore it
Selects everything in the field, ready to cut, copy or replace
Deletes; double-tap and hold to keep deleting
☰ is always the menu. The keys right of Voice stay put while you dictate. Hold any of these keys on the bar (or swipe up from it) to pick another on the spot; picking only sets it.
Types your most recent dictation again, as it was typed: handy when it went into the wrong box or got sent too soon
Off. Tap to turn on Voicebar in Accessibility settings (if Android says it\'s restricted, allow restricted settings in the app\'s App info first).
Gboard isn\'t turned on as a keyboard. Tap to open keyboard settings.
Turn on Gboard in Android\'s keyboard settings first

Voicebar\'s companion. Over Gboard it shows a button that switches back to Voicebar, and listens for “voice bar” there. While you dictate it reads the text on screen once, so names come out spelled as they appear, and it notices when you fix a word Voicebar typed, to learn it. In hands-free mode (“voice bar, hands free”) it reads the screen and taps, types and scrolls where you say. It never reads password fields. What it reads goes only to Claude, with your own key, and only while you\'re dictating or using hands-free.
A strip in Gboard\'s own color, joined to its top edge, that says Tap to return
Covers Gboard\'s voice key wherever Gboard puts it. With Gboard\'s voice key off, it takes the right-hand mirror of Gboard\'s ⊞ button, if that spot is free.
A mic bubble above Gboard; drag it anywhere
Turned on. Hold ABC to switch to it for typing.

Tap Cursor for a trackpad: drag to move the cursor, hold still then drag to select, and keep one finger down while another drags to go further. Cut, copy, paste and delete sit above it. Tap Done to fold it away.

Undo, cut, copy, paste and select all; paste what\'s on the clipboard, from any app; your recent dictations; docked or floating (and, floating, shrinking it to the record pill); another keyboard; and settings.

Tap ABC and Voicebar\'s keyboard pops up: suggestions across the top, hold a key for its accents or number, slide on space to move the cursor, double-tap shift for caps lock. It takes over the bar\'s row, so its bottom row is the usual one, with ⋮ next to ?123 for the bar\'s menu (hold it for Gboard). Pull the handle at the top down to put the voice bar back. Hold ABC and Gboard takes over instead (Look switches the two). Tap to return on Gboard (or the mic in its voice-key spot, or the floating mic) brings Voicebar back, already listening.

Say \"title case\", the words, then \"end title case\": The Lord of the Rings. Say \"quote\" … \"end quote\" for quotation marks and \"open paren\" … \"close paren\" for parentheses. Quotes and parentheses need both ends (so \"get me a quote\" stays words); title case ends by itself when you finish. Say \"literal quote\" for the word.
Turn on the way back from Gboard

When you start talking, the app\'s name and its latest text (the chat you\'re replying to, say) go to Claude\'s final cleanup, so names are spelled as they appear there and sound-alikes are read in context. Speech recognition never sees it, and the text doesn\'t change while you talk. The whole screen needs the Gboard button (accessibility) on; without it, only the text box is used. Password fields are never read.
Listen as soon as a text box opens

Dictation starts by itself whenever you tap into a text field, as if you\'d tapped Voice. If nobody talks at the phone in the first few seconds, it stops. Not in password fields, and not while a physical keyboard is connected.
Way back from Gboard is off. Tap to turn it on
From now on, “%1$s” is written like that · tap to undo
Couldn\'t find Send: your message is still in the box, and copied
No commands for 5 minutes · hands-free off
Set up speech recognition first: an ElevenLabs key or Parakeet
Couldn\'t work that out · try again
No text box to type in
Cursor’s in the middle · “cursor up”, then “tap”
Hands-free needs the Gboard button (accessibility) on

Say “voice bar, hands free” (or use the Quick Settings tile) to control the phone by voice: “tap Send”, “scroll down”, “type …”, “open Spotify”, “show numbers” then “tap 7”, “go ahead and reply to Siona saying I\'m late”. A cursor shows each tap. Sending, buying or deleting waits for “yes”. Say “stop” or tap the pill to end. Needs the accessibility service; streams to ElevenLabs while on (about $0.39 an hour) and turns off after 5 quiet minutes.
Also listen for “voice bar, hands free” when no keyboard is up, on the phone, with the model above. Uses some battery and keeps the microphone indicator on.

tap / click / long press <name or number> · show numbers · hide numbers · scroll up/down (a bit · half a screen · one full screen · two pages · a lot · to the top · all the way down) · page up/down · swipe left/right · zoom in/out · type <words> · clear · focus the search box · open <app or thing on screen> · go back · go home · recent apps · notifications · quick settings · cursor up/down/left/right (a bit) · cursor to <name> · tap · go ahead and <goal> · yes · no · stop. Anything else is worked out by Claude.
Skipped · you can add it in Settings
Talk instead of type. A one-row voice bar that sits under your apps; Gboard stays around for typing.
Voicebar for talking, Gboard for typing, one tap apart
Used only while you talk to it
ElevenLabs hears you; Claude tidies the words (optional). You pay them directly, usually pennies
Optional: a way back from Gboard, and hands-free control
About three minutes. Everything here can be changed later in Settings.
In the list that opens, turn on Voicebar, and Gboard if it\'s off. Then come back here.
Turn it on in the list
Not installed: Voicebar uses it for typing

Android warns that a keyboard can collect what you type. Voicebar doesn\'t record typing: it sends what you say to ElevenLabs, and the words to Claude for cleanup, with your own keys. Nothing goes anywhere else.
Pick Voicebar in the list that pops up. It\'ll be the keyboard you see first.
The keyboard button on the bar switches to Gboard; the Gboard button (later) brings you back
Voicebar listens only when you ask it to.
While you\'re dictating, or in hands-free mode; the bar shows it every time
Listening for the wake word happens on the phone; nothing is sent until you start talking to it
Voicebar uses ElevenLabs to hear you, with your own API key. It costs about $0.39 per hour of talking.
Make a free account; speech to text is billed by the hour as you use it
Opens Developers › API Keys. Tap Create, give it Speech to Text access, then copy it.
The key is checked with ElevenLabs, then kept on this phone, encrypted. It\'s never sent anywhere but ElevenLabs.
Or keep it on the phone
Ready · used instead of ElevenLabs; change it any time in Settings
Parakeet needs no key or account and works offline. Words come in short bursts rather than live, and it\'s English only. Cleanup (next) still uses Claude if you add a key.
Claude fixes punctuation, drops the ums and spells your names right. Optional, but it\'s what makes the text sound like you wrote it.
“um so meet at the camel back trail head at six forty no wait seven”
Meet at the Camelback trailhead at 7.
New to the Claude API? Sign up
Opens the Claude Console. API use is separate from a Claude.ai Pro or Max plan
The API is pay as you go: a few dollars of credit lasts a long time for cleanup
Opens Settings › API keys. Tap Create key, then copy it (it starts with sk-ant-).
Uses Claude Haiku: a fraction of a cent per message. Kept on this phone, encrypted, and sent only to Anthropic.
Optional. Turn on Voicebar in Accessibility to put a button on Gboard that brings you back, and to unlock hands-free control.
Android blocks this for apps installed from a file, like this one. Allow it once:
Try turning Voicebar on in Accessibility first
In App info, tap ⋮ and then Allow restricted settings
Come back and turn it on again
A mic button on Gboard that switches back to Voicebar
“Voice bar, hands free”: tap, scroll and type by voice
Reads the screen as you start talking, and learns from your fixes in Gboard

Accessibility lets Voicebar see and act on what\'s on screen. It reads the screen only while you dictate or use hands-free, never password fields, and sends it only to ElevenLabs and Claude with your keys.
Tap any text box and Voicebar comes up. Tap the mic and talk.
Run this again any time from Settings › Help.
The key works, but couldn\'t be saved on this phone
Permissions, keyboards and API keys, step by step
A key is saved · paste a new one to replace it
Paste your key; it\'s checked before it\'s saved
They\'ll pick up where you left off next time the bar opens. You can also find them in Settings › Help.
A short tour of the bar when it first opens, with Back and Next
Start over from the first tip
Done · the tour starts next time the bar opens
Words go straight into the box as you speak. Pause, and what you said gets tidied up.
Or swipe the pill right to finish and send, left to throw it away. ⌫ still works while you talk.
Tap ABC for Voicebar\'s keyboard; pull its handle down to bring the bar back. Hold ABC to switch to Gboard; the mic button on Gboard brings you back here.
Tap for a trackpad with select all, cut, copy and paste. Or slide along the Voice pill.
Tap ⌫ for one letter; tap then hold to clear words fast.
Then “send”, “done”, “cancel” or “close”. “Voice bar, hands free” controls the whole phone by voice.
In the cloud with your key: words appear as you speak, about $0.39 an hour, many languages
Private, free, offline · English · %1$d MB download
Downloaded · nothing you say leaves the phone. Words come in short bursts as you talk
Downloading… %1$d of %2$d MB (you can leave this screen)
Other voices nearby, a TV or a conversation, are silenced before speech recognition hears them. Adds about half a second
Optional · without one, the first voice at the phone is kept. Record one (about 30 seconds of reading) to always know yours
Stronger silences more of other voices, but may drop some of yours, in noise or when you whisper
No voiceprint: when you tap Voice, the first voice talking at the phone is kept and other voices are silenced. Record a voiceprint to make it always yours
%1$s · %2$d MB download, runs on the phone
Downloaded · nothing you say leaves the phone for this
Somewhere quiet, hold the phone as you usually do and read these aloud at your normal pace. Only you should be talking.
Saved. Voicebar will listen for this voice
Saved, but the recording was uneven. If voices get dropped, record again somewhere quieter
That wasn’t enough speech; try again and read all the sentences
Allow the microphone on the Voice page first
Talk, then have someone else talk or play a video. The bar shows how much it sounds like you; past the line, it’s heard.

The voiceprint is a list of numbers describing how your voice sounds, made and kept on this phone and never uploaded. Voices talking at the very same moment as you can’t be separated; this handles other people speaking between your words, TV, and conversations nearby.
On a tablet or an unfolded phone, keep the bar\'s buttons together at one side, where your thumb reaches. On narrower screens the bar always uses its whole width.
Tap to copy the report (what went wrong, where in the code, and the version) to paste into a message. It\'s kept only on this phone.
A minute, narrated: talking, tidying, finishing, Gboard, the cursor, commands and hands-free

A child talking between your words is silenced before speech recognition hears it: a small child\'s voice is far higher than an adult\'s. Nothing to set up, works on the phone, adds a twentieth of a second. If they talk over you, cleanup also drops obvious interruptions
How high counts as a child
Stronger catches older children with lower voices, but may silence adults with high voices
The old Voicebar is still installed. Android treats this one as a new app, so move your settings, dictionary and voiceprint across, then remove the old one.
In the old Voicebar, tap Export settings
Saves your settings, dictionary (with what it learned), voiceprint and usage to a file. Not your API keys.
Loads a file you exported, replacing these settings, the dictionary and the voiceprint.
Settings imported: %1$d dictionary words, %2$s. Add your API keys under Voice.
Paste an OpenAI API key (platform.openai.com › API keys). It\'s used for cleanup with GPT-6 Luna (choose it under Model), and stored encrypted on this phone.
Cleaning up again needs a Claude or OpenAI key
Add a Claude or OpenAI key to tidy up what you say
Not listening by itself: a keyboard is connected and the phone is lying still. Tap Voice to talk, or pick the phone up.
Say what\'s wrong in the box (\"drop the okay at the end\"), hand edits and all, and it\'s fixed. What you say is never typed. Holding Voice does this too
Nothing in the box to fix yet
No text box to fix here
Too much in this box to fix by voice
Finish this dictation first, then fix it
Fixed, and copied: the box changed while it was being fixed

When you swipe to send, %1$s gives the whole message one last read and fixes only what pauses leave behind: a capital in the middle of a sentence, a sentence split in two, a stray word like a trailing “okay”. It never rewords or adds anything; otherwise the message goes as it was.

When you swipe to send and the app\'s Send button has no label, %1$s picks it from a picture of the buttons beside the message box (which shows your message). If that sends it, the button is remembered for that app; if a remembered button stops working, it\'s forgotten.
Needs a Claude or OpenAI key, above.
Add an OpenAI key to use this
Add a Claude key to use this
The last 5 minutes, to copy into a bug report
What Voicebar is built with, and their licenses
Voicebar is built with these, made by others and shared under their licenses. Tap one for its license.

Voicebar\'s own events (fields opening, dictation, the auto-listen check, cleanup at pauses and at the end, what the voice filters silenced, Send) with short excerpts of what was said, then Android\'s log for the app: its warnings and errors, or everything it logged. Only the last 5 minutes, only on this phone; nothing is sent unless you paste it somewhere.
What Voicebar did in the last 5 minutes (with short excerpts of what was said), to paste into a bug report. Kept only in memory, never sent anywhere.

When auto-listen starts in a messaging or email app, words show in the bar instead of the message until you finish, and if it ends on its own they wait for a tap. It also stops after a minute untouched.
Not cleaned up (%1$s), typed as spoken
Not cleaned up (%1$s), so not sent: typed as spoken
No text box selected: copied to the clipboard
Can\'t press Send: the Gboard button is off (your message is kept and copied). Tap to turn it back on
Android switched off the Gboard button. Tap to turn it back on
The Gboard button stopped running. Tap, then turn it off and on again
Let it run in the background, so Android doesn\'t stop it to save battery and switch this button off
Allowed · Android won\'t stop it to save battery
Allowed (battery optimization off), so Android won\'t stop it or switch off the Gboard button
